newsitem.title: USA: Green issues seen slowing U.S. electricity law.
newsitem.headline: Green issues seen slowing U.S. electricity law.

text.p: Federal deregulation of the electricity industry could encounter long delays if environmental issues are given a role in development of a restructuring legislation, industry officials said Tuesday.

"If you really think you can put a small environmental title on an industry structure bill and get it through anytime soon, I think you have totally misread the politics," said Bob Beck, vice president for environmental affairs of the Edison Electric Institute, a group representing electrical utilities.

"I think it will be just as bitter as it was for the entire decade of the '80s," Beck said, referring to drawn-out debate toward passage of federal clean-air legislation in 1990. He spoke to reporters during an annual meeting of the institute.
The Clinton administration is expected to submit by next month its proposed blueprint for deregulating the electricity industry -- a process already begun by individual states.
Energy Secretary Federico Pena told the convention Monday that enviromental issues were "inseparable" from the debate over electricity policy.
Federal restructuring law should promote sustainable energy goals, energy efficiency, and renewable energy technology, he said.
"I, like most Americans, believe that our air and water and land should be cleaner, and electricity restructuring should be part of the solution, not part of the problem," Pena said.
The institute is opposed to inclusion of an environmental plank in the bill.
Interests active in the clean-air legislation debate already were gearing up to participate in the restructuring bill, Beck said.

"You can already see it begin to become the big issue," he said. "We still talk about stranded costs. We still talk about market power. But all of a sudden, transport, clean air, ... emissions ... are beginning to almost overwhelm all those other issues."
"That is not what I think the purpose of the legislation is going to be. The purpose of the legislation is to try to restructure the electric utility industry."
He said a more appropriate forum for environmental issues would be in the Clean Air Act, which comes up for renewal this November. ((--Randall Mikkelsen, Philadelphia Newsroom, 215-972-0618 x 18))
